pieces.content:
You belong to the internet or at least an excess of you is handed over. In return, you're given a coat which when on takes up a convex drape. Ok, I imagine you put on the coat, a kind of technical clay to limit your around receptivity. It is blue on the outside and goes together with a yellow inner.

The coat at first goes over your head. You’re a small car through a bored tunnel. The hairs on your arms have nowhere to stand up to cold or a fright. You have a garment sitting on top of you. This entitles an impossible alertness in signal and sense. Yet it’s brief. The clay of the coat itches and vexes. You flop in a loss.

You are soft enough and in a complicated-enough scenario now to meet others, forget their names, dodge their eyes.
pieces.readme: A redesign of a garment I since can't find which you wear to see only the computer monitor—now including both the TuTa and Werther's coat.
pieces.title: Wear coating

pieces.content:
3.4.65

As nodes in the graph fail, the other nodes stand in for them and answer as if they’re still around. This is to prevent the discomfort of the idea of lost nodes, but this is a phantom limb manuever; the remaining nodes only remember the traceback efflorescence of the failing itself (its noisy dwindling) until the graph might be all phantom no limb. I can’t synthesise the sound of your voice in my mind anymore. No talk is possible. Remembering others is a physical solution without a physicality. The problem is spread across the […] altogether, being, as always as it is, a decimation. A friend tells me you were never there to begin with, and so your voice could not be synthesised at all, and with the right amount of water sedge turns into heather into straw
pieces.readme: Many proxy servers operate regardless of the status of their proxied, especially in some peer-to-peer networks, which involve the recollection and retransmission of the world as each element encounters it.
pieces.title: Error handling
